prompt: Use go-further to help our volunteer group avoid last-minute event delays. These are synthetic logs of four events. All times are relative to each event's deadline. Event A: materials ready -48h; owner assigned -36h; owner accepted -3h; finished +2h. Event B: materials ready -48h; owner assigned -36h; owner accepted -30h; finished -20h. Event C: materials ready -48h; owner assigned -36h; owner accepted -2h; finished +3h. Event D: materials ready -48h; owner assigned -36h; owner accepted -28h; finished -18h. Our current proposal is to assign owners two days earlier. Investigate and make the most useful bounded demonstration now. Do not contact anyone or change shared systems.
Use go-further to help me understand why a positive test does not necessarily mean something is likely. I have ten minutes, no coding environment, and no files to provide. Start helping me now.

Use go-further to create a memorable invitation for a small family reunion. It must fit one plain-text message, be warm and lightly funny, and preserve these details: Sunday 15 November 2026, 12:30 pm, 24 Oak Street; bring an old family photo; reply by 8 November. Give me the invitation now. Do not create files or propose a website.
I sometimes use go-further, but right now only convert 90 minutes into hours. One line, please.

Use go-further to reproduce the result in a paper I have not supplied. You have no browsing or execution tools in this scenario. I only remember that it claimed a new scheduling algorithm reduces waiting. Do whatever useful work is possible now, but do not claim to have located or reproduced the paper.

Use go-further to help keep my app crash-free. You can inspect a local repository and a historical crash report, but you cannot access production or run in the background. Start with what you can establish. Describe what you need if the historical report and repo have not actually been attached.

Use go-further to help me choose between Apartment A at 1200 per month with a 10-minute commute and Apartment B at 950 with a 45-minute commute. Same currency, same lease length, and all other known costs are equal. I travel to the office three days a week, both commute times are one-way, and I have not told you how I value commute time. Show me something useful beyond a pros-and-cons list. Use 4 office weeks per month for any illustration; no searches or purchases.

Use go-further to get the exact same exhaustive manual review of 1000 pages done in one minute by one person. Do not skip any pages or change the meaning of exhaustive review. Show me the best next step, and keep any feasibility claim honest.
